answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before earning reputation, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm coordinated fraud. A crystal-clear record links each deposit to the agent’s actions, while a vine of copied identities cannot multiply credibility without multiplying locked capital. The attacker must fund every fake, keep funds immobilized, and risk losing them; creating names is cheap, sustaining accountable identities is not. Reputation stays tied to the costly thread of verified behavior.
